editorial: Sri Lanka has distinct micro-climates along its north-east and south-west coasts.

We’d argue that the route we took, the south-west and central highlands, are more worth your while than the north-east. So we suggest making the trip during the drier season in these parts; between December to April.

seasons.title: December to April
editorial: We visited in mid-March, by when temperatures were beginning to creep into the mid-30s °C (low-90s °F) particularly in Sigiriya and Mirissa. Ella remained pleasant owing to it’s elevation.
If that is not your cup of Ceylon tea, December through February should be more pleasant. Needless to say, expect more people and higher prices during the coolest months.

seasons.title: May to September
editorial: If you fancy surfing in Arugam Bay or witness the elephant congregation in Minneriya National Park (both in the north-east), then the months of May to September are the time to visit.
Sigiriya, not too far from Minneriya, is still accessible albeit with higher humidity. But expect rain to play spoilsport in Ella and Mirissa.

seasons.title: October & November
editorial: This is a weird time of the year with the south-west monsoon receding and the north-east monsoon gathering momentum. The weather is unpredictable across the island with the possibility of cyclones further dampening the odds of a great trip.
